findings.title: Unique index that includes but does not lead with tenant_id is reported
findings.detail: The spec reports a unique index or foreign key 'that does not lead with or include tenant_id'. The code requires a unique index to lead with tenant_id (indkey[0]), but accepts a foreign key that includes tenant_id at any position. So a UNIQUE (email, tenant_id) index is reported, while the 'or include' wording could be read as allowing it. No scenario pins this case down.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN an otherwise compliant table has a unique constraint on (email, tenant_id) THEN checkTenancyCatalog reports unique_not_tenant_leading for that constraint's index.

findings.title: Five-letter Node error codes are mistaken for SQLSTATEs in ensureDefaultTenant
findings.detail: sqlState() accepts any code matching /^[0-9A-Z]{5}$/. A Node system error such as EPIPE or EPERM therefore becomes TENANT_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED with details.sqlstate 'EPIPE' instead of propagating. Task 5.1 says only a pg error carrying a SQLSTATE maps, and other errors propagate.
findings.suggested_fix: Map only errors that are pg DatabaseError instances (or that carry a severity field) to TENANT_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED.

findings.title: A failed tenant reset after a successful COMMIT rejects although the writes were committed
findings.detail: In inTransaction, when COMMIT succeeds but the following `set_config('app.tenant_id', '', false)` throws (for example the connection drops between the two statements), `failure` is set to the reset error. withTenantTx then rejects even though fn's writes are durable. A caller that retries on rejection may duplicate the work. No scenario pins down what the helper should report in this case.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN the session reset after a successful COMMIT fails THEN withTenantTx destroys the connection and rejects with the reset's error even though fn's writes are committed.

findings.title: fn issuing its own COMMIT or ROLLBACK is not detected
findings.detail: If fn runs `ROLLBACK` (or `COMMIT`) itself, the helper's later COMMIT runs outside a transaction and Postgres answers with a warning and tag COMMIT, not ROLLBACK. withTenantTx then resolves with fn's result. Any statements fn ran after its own ROLLBACK ran in autocommit with no transaction-local tenant set. No scenario covers this.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN fn itself runs ROLLBACK and returns a value THEN withTenantTx resolves with that value, and its own COMMIT reports no transaction in progress.

findings.title: Unique index that includes but does not lead with tenant_id is reported
findings.detail: The spec reports a unique index or foreign key 'that does not lead with or include tenant_id'. The code requires a unique index to lead with tenant_id (indkey[0]), but accepts a foreign key that includes tenant_id at any position. So a UNIQUE (email, tenant_id) index is reported, while the 'or include' wording could be read as allowing it. No scenario pins this case down.
evidence: src/tenancy/catalog.ts: WHERE (c.tenant_attnum IS NOT NULL AND i.indkey[0] = c.tenant_attnum) IS NOT TRUE
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN an otherwise compliant table has a unique constraint on (email, tenant_id) THEN checkTenancyCatalog reports unique_not_tenant_leading for that constraint's index.

findings.title: Five-letter Node error codes are mistaken for SQLSTATEs in ensureDefaultTenant
findings.detail: sqlState() accepts any code matching /^[0-9A-Z]{5}$/. A Node system error such as EPIPE or EPERM therefore becomes TENANT_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED with details.sqlstate 'EPIPE' instead of propagating. Task 5.1 says only a pg error carrying a SQLSTATE maps, and other errors propagate.
findings.suggested_fix: Map only errors that are pg DatabaseError instances (or that carry a severity field) to TENANT_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED.

findings.title: A failed tenant reset after a successful COMMIT rejects although the writes were committed
findings.detail: In inTransaction, when COMMIT succeeds but the following `set_config('app.tenant_id', '', false)` throws (for example the connection drops between the two statements), `failure` is set to the reset error. withTenantTx then rejects even though fn's writes are durable. A caller that retries on rejection may duplicate the work. No scenario pins down what the helper should report in this case.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN the session reset after a successful COMMIT fails THEN withTenantTx destroys the connection and rejects with the reset's error even though fn's writes are committed.

findings.title: fn issuing its own COMMIT or ROLLBACK is not detected
findings.detail: If fn runs `ROLLBACK` (or `COMMIT`) itself, the helper's later COMMIT runs outside a transaction and Postgres answers with a warning and tag COMMIT, not ROLLBACK. withTenantTx then resolves with fn's result. Any statements fn ran after its own ROLLBACK ran in autocommit with no transaction-local tenant set. No scenario covers this.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN fn itself runs ROLLBACK and returns a value THEN withTenantTx resolves with that value, and its own COMMIT reports no transaction in progress.

riskiest_assumptions: That src/tenancy/tx.ts (part 2) runs set_config before fn and resets the tenant afterwards, which the passes of C-f6d2db43 and C-96d545df partly rely on through the gate's tx.test results.
That assertTenantContext in context.ts (part 1, not shown) rejects exactly the three invalid contexts. I rely on the passing spy test for this.
That src/tenancy/index.ts (not in the diff) already re-exports every symbol the tests import, as the gate's passing typecheck and tests suggest.
